subject.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.list[].tools.agentToAgent.allow` now as the per-agent outbound A2A authorization contract, or defer it to the broader session-visibility permission model?
rationale: The PR adds a user-facing config knob and SDK-visible authorization decision for cross-agent session tools, so outbound-only semantics and upgrade/security expectations need maintainer intent beyond the mechanical normalization repair.

options.title: Accept Narrow Outbound Override After Repair
options.body: Normalize exact allow entries, resolve conflicts, and land the focused outbound-only contract while broader session visibility remains separate.

options.title: Defer To Broader Permission Design
options.body: Pause or close this branch and fold the A2A semantics into the broader per-agent session visibility work tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59149 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48785.

options.title: Require Receiver-Side Semantics First
options.body: Ask for an explicit design covering outbound-only versus bidirectional or `receivesFrom` behavior before accepting any new config surface.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Outbound Override After Repair
recommendation.body: Normalize exact allow entries, resolve conflicts, and land the focused outbound-only contract while broader session visibility remains separate.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points most strongly to steipete for the session-tool authorization/config boundary and related product-security tradeoff.
